Omar Alzori · linkedin.com/in/omarmudhaffarSeptember 2026
The idea
01 / 07
Most of us like sport

Few of us keep a plan.

📄
The plan lives in a PDF
You download the perfect program. It dies in your Downloads folder, next to 14 other PDFs you will definitely read.
🤷
Nobody tracks it
"What did you lift last week?" "A lot." "How much protein?" "Yes." After a month nobody knows, so nobody improves.
💸
A real coach costs money
The people who fix this charge more per month than your rent. Fine, than your food. Still no.

Heaft puts that coach in your phone. Free for the plan, the session, and your friends.

The app
02 / 07
What it does

Tell it your goal. It does the rest.

✨
Your coach builds the plan
Four questions. A full program in thirty seconds.
⏱️
It runs your session
Log the set. The rest timer starts itself.
🥑
Food that fits the day
Calories and protein from your steps and your lifts.
🔥
Progress you can see
Streaks, personal records, the weight going up.
Why it works
03 / 07
The loop

Every week it learns you a bit more.

1
Plan
Four questions become a program built for your days and your gym.
2
Train
Sets, weights, rest and how hard it felt, captured while you lift.
3
Data
Steps, meals and lifts in one place instead of four different apps.
4
Adapt
Next week the weights and the calories move with what you actually did.

Who I need
05 / 07
Where you fit

Join me for three weeks. Leave with more than a grade.

🧪
QA tester
You wake up at 7, come to the gym with me for free, and we run real test scenarios on real sets. You break it before users do.
You learnWriting real test cases and bug reports, running a sprint on ClickUp, and writing an SRS a team can build from.
🚀
Entrepreneur
You convince people to use it and work out how we sell it. If you can sell a gym membership in January, you can sell this.
You learnHow a product gets priced, positioned and put in front of real users — and how to read what they do, not what they say.
🎨
UI/UX designer
You make it feel great: onboarding, the session screen, the share cards. My buttons are fine. Yours will be better.
You learnWhat a design system really is — tokens, components, states — and how to drive Figma with AI so you ship faster.
💻
Developer
You build features next to me, we review each other’s code, and we ship something every single week.
You learnSystem architecture, prompt engineering, CI/CD and deploys. How to be an engineer, not just a vibe coder.
📊
Data analyst
The app already logs every set, meal and step. Nobody has looked at it yet. Bring a laptop, not a barbell.
You learnDesigning what gets logged, querying a live production database, and turning raw events into numbers a team acts on.
